title: LLM probe diary — micro-quant + prompt A/B
content:
Quick log of small experiments I ran while triaging odd generation artifacts + latency spikes. Mostly scratch — rough notes, hypotheses, CLI commands to re-run, and immediate next steps.

Date: 2026-04-02
Context: lightweight nightly micro-bench against v2-7B (float16 and 4-bit SGQ) on a single A100-80GB - using local dev pool. Trying to reproduce a jittery tail latency observed in canary traffic. Also exploring a compact prompt A/B to validate suffix truncation effects.

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Models: rwinf/v2-7b-fp16, rwinf/v2-7b-sgq4
- Prompt variants: A (full system + 3-shot), B (system trimmed, 1-shot, suffix pruning)
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8 (micro-batch pipeline)
- KV cache: enabled/disabled; test with small session-lengths (50, 200 tokens)
- Batching policy: continuous batching ON with max_wait_ms=15 vs OFF (immediate)
- Quant knobs: per-channel scale vs global scale for SGQ, fallback to fp16 on cross-attn kernels

Notes / Observations:
- Baseline (fp16, batch=1, KV on): median latency 78ms/token, p95 165ms. Stable.
- SGQ4 (batch=1, KV on): median 86ms/token, p95 310ms. Heavy p95 increase — likely fallback paths on certain attention dims.
- Enabling continuous batching (max_wait_ms=15) smoothed median slightly for batch=4 but increased p95 for SGQ4 by ~30ms compared to immediate. Hypothesis: batching triggers different kernel selection causing slow fallback for some sequence lengths.
- KV disabled reduces p95 for SGQ4 by ~60ms but increases median by ~10ms (less re-use across tokens). So there's a trade: KV -> median down, tail up (for quant).
- Prompt B (suffix pruning) reduced average generated tokens by 12% and lowered p95 by ~8% on fp16; on SGQ4 effect similar but less pronounced. Seems content truncation reduces some expensive cross-attention patterns.

Weird artifact: SGQ4 sometimes emits repeated punctuation sequences ("!!!
!!!
") on iter 3+ when long context with many short examples. Repro steps: run prompt A with 3 varied examples, 512 context, temperature 0.8, top_k=40; seed fixed. Repeatable ~7/10. Not seen on fp16.
Hypothesis: quantized cross-attention accumulation underflows or round-off causes token scoring spikes. Try forcing fallback for cross-attention to fp16 (quick patch) and re-run.

Commands to re-run the failing case (local dev):
- python experiments/run_probe.py --model rwinf/v2-7b-sgq4 --prompt variants/promptA.json --temp 0.8 --top_k 40 --context_len 512 --seed 42 --kv on --batch 1 --profile tail
- curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -d '@payload.json' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' (payload.json contains same prompt + params)

Profile snippets (from quick perf log):
- run 2026-04-02T09:22:16Z: p50=84ms, p90=190ms, p95=312ms, mem=26.8GB
- run 2026-04-02T09:48:05Z (kv off): p50=95ms, p90=170ms, p95=255ms, mem=24.1GB
- run 2026-04-02T10:05:42Z (continuous batching, max_wait=15): p50=78ms, p90=205ms, p95=340ms, mem=27.9GB

Quick ideas tested (notes):
- Force fp16 for cross-attention kernels only -> removes punctuation-repeat artifact. Needs bench on longer runs.
- Adjust continuous batching policy to dynamic max_wait (grow/shrink based on recent latency) to avoid batch-induced slow kernel paths.
- Try per-head scale SGQ variant (local patch) — plausible improvement on tail.
- Introduce small jitter in request arrival during microbench to simulate realistic traffic (I added sleep(random.uniform(0,0.02))). It changed p95 behavior slightly — needs more runs.

To-do (short):
- [ ] Re-run repeating-punct artifact with cross-attn forced-fp16 + SGQ4, collect 100 seeds (priority high).
- [ ] File a minimal reproducer and add to GH PR notes for model onboarding (link to PR in linked_artifacts).
- [ ] Try per-head SGQ patch (#local-phi) on 2026-04-04 morning slot.
- [ ] Add a quick unit test to the kernel selector that asserts consistent kernel choice for identical seq_len distribution (low-effort guard).
- [ ] Run a small canary against Dedicated cluster with identical config to see if this is infra-specific.

Open questions / scribbles:
- Is the repeat-punct purely numerical (quant) or an interaction with tokenization when many short examples are present? Could try marginally perturbing examples (whitespace) to test.
- Should we prefer kv disabled for SGQ profiles in the model catalog as a temporary safety? Cost vs UX trade-off.
- Idea: prefix-pruning-as-cache-heuristic — maintain small LRU of recent KV prefixes across requests; drop unlikely prefixes if tail latency grows. Sketch seems reasonable; long-term research.

Notes to self on data collection format: keep CSV columns: date,model,quant,kv,continuous_batch,max_wait,batch,p50,p90,p95,mem,artifact_flag,seed. Save as experiments/llm-microbench-2026-04.csv and push to GH for tracking.

Last minute: ping Jun to see if he wants me to run the SGQ per-head variant overnight on ci-gpu-small. Ava: can you add the reproducer payload to the JIRA ticket?

End of entry.

-- miles
